newsitem.title: USA: TAG Heuer sees $25 mln franc charge in '97.
newsitem.headline: TAG Heuer sees $25 mln franc charge in '97.

text.p: TAG Heuer International SA said Monday that it will incur a charge in 1997 of 25 million Swiss francs in connection with the reintegration of inventory previously sold to World Commerce Corp, currently its exclusive distributor in Japan.
The company said that it has signed an agreement with World Commerce to transfer the portion of its business that distributes watches to TAG Heuer Japan KK, a new subsidiary.
TAG Heuer said the transaction is valued at 90 million Swiss francs. The company said the deal further consolidates its potential to obtain higher returns in its key markets.

In other news, the company said that results for 1997 will be affected by this acquisition, the lauch of a major new watch series and poor trading in duty free sales and reduced Japanese spending, which are negatively affecting markets in Hong Kong and Australia.
The company also said the refinancing of $71.5 million in notes would positively affect the rest of the year. TAG Heuer is a designer of Swiss sports watches and chronographs.
